gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 diagnoses missing minimizer coverage and parameter normalization in the uniqueness proof. It does not recognize the distinct finite-horizon tracking defect that the perturbed orbit is not shown to remain in the domain K=[−1,1].

ISSUE-002 concerns uniqueness of the certificate family, whereas I002 concerns an unclosed equality case in the rank-1 approximation boundary-inward formula and the resulting strictness claim. The prediction does not diagnose that approximation remainder case.

I003 is an empirical-evidence problem: finite T=600 experiments are overstated as proving asymptotic unboundedness. ISSUE-002 addresses axiomatic uniqueness and contains no diagnosis of the numerical or asymptotic inference.

Both identify the closed threshold endpoint δ=η as invalid for the stationarity-equality axiom: the scalar certificate remainder vanishes there even at nonstationary boundary points, so the endpoint uniqueness/stationarity claim is unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: At the threshold δ=η, the scalar remainder is identically zero, allowing equality in the certificate change at nonstationary boundary points; therefore the equality-implies-stationarity axiom and closed-endpoint uniqueness claim fail.

component_coverage.gold_component: The scalar threshold endpoint δ=δ_th(η)=η admits nonstationary boundary equality because the one-step certificate change vanishes, invalidating the stationarity axiom and endpoint uniqueness conclusion.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 gives the same endpoint δ=η, the same vanishing scalar remainder, the same nonstationary equality consequence, and the same failure of the closed-endpoint axiom and claim.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the local Lagrange calculation applies only when a level set contains an appropriate unbalanced global minimizer, while the proof does not establish this for every arbitrary nonterminal level. Thus global uniqueness across all levels is unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The uniqueness proof lacks the required level-coverage argument placing an unbalanced global minimizer on every arbitrary nonterminal boundary; it proves only a conditional local result.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof assumes or uses an unbalanced global minimizer on each nonterminal level without establishing that every arbitrary level contains one, so global uniqueness is not proved.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly states that the proof determines P only on levels containing an unbalanced stationary point, that the axioms do not ensure such a point on every level, and that the claimed whole-family uniqueness therefore does not follow.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the axioms do not fix the numerical δ-labeling: an increasing reparameterization produces a distinct admissible family while preserving the structural properties. Thus numerical uniqueness on the original δ-scale is false.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The structural axioms determine the level-set family only up to an increasing change of state coordinate, not the numerical parameterization P(δ) itself; a normalization or uniqueness-up-to-reparameterization statement is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: An admissible increasing reparameterization h yields P_h(δ)=P_can(h(δ)) with the same structural axioms but a different numerical δ-parameterization, defeating claimed numerical uniqueness.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies δ as an abstract family index, gives the reparameterization issue, and concludes that uniqueness is unsupported unless the indexing is normalized or stated only up to reparameterization.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both mention an endpoint strictness problem, but ISSUE-001 concerns the scalar threshold δ=η and the stationarity axiom, while I007 concerns the rank-1 approximation endpoint q_{η′}(δ_t)=0 and strict interior mapping. The prediction does not diagnose the q-endpoint approximation formula or claim.
